Strengthening exercises support the hip by building muscles that stabilize the joint, which can ease pain, slow further deterioration, and make daily tasks easier, [0, 1]. Simple at-home strengthening options include repeated sit-to-stand from a chair without using the hands, wall-supported shallow squats to about a 30-degree knee bend, and single-leg standing with support as needed, all of which build lower-body strength and balance relevant to hip stability,, [0, 1, 2]. Range-of-motion and flexibility exercises reduce stiffness and help restore mobility, and they can be started a few times per week and progressed to daily as tolerated [2]. For the hip, examples include a supported forward lunge with the front knee not passing the toes and a lying knee-to-chest stretch, each held briefly and repeated for sets to improve motion and comfort [2]. Similar home routines recommended for hip OA include low-impact activities (walking, stationary cycling, swimming, yoga), targeted strengthening (chair stands, bridges, hip extensions), and flexibility drills (inner thigh stretches and hip rotations) to improve pain and range of motion while protecting the joint [5]. Research supports exercise as a core non-drug treatment for hip and knee osteoarthritis, with evidence that programs including walking, biking, running when appropriate, aquatic exercise, and core strengthening improve function, redistribute mechanical stress away from the hip, and enhance overall health outcomes like sleep and posture,, [3, 4, 6]. A structured, multimodal physiotherapy approach that combines targeted exercises with manual therapy and education is being evaluated in rigorous randomized, placebo-controlled trials, reflecting typical clinical practice and aiming to reduce pain and improve function in hip OA beyond exercise alone, [8, 9]. If you are just starting, choose low-impact options, progress gradually, include strengthening and daily range-of-motion work, and consider consulting a clinician or arthritis-focused class to tailor exercises safely to your symptoms and goals,, [0, 1, 2].
